title: NTA UGC NET English Full Mock Test #14
subtitle: 100 Questions · 200 Marks · Post-2018 NTA Pattern · Zero Answer Bias (25 A/B/C/D) · Reading Comprehension (Q91-100)

items.title: Mock #14 · Q1
items.stem:
Match List I with List II:

List I (Work)
A. The Nutmeg's Curse: Parables for a Planet in Crisis
B. Victory City
C. A Time Outside This Time: A Novel
D. Translating Myself and Others

List II (Author)
I. Amitava Kumar
II. Amitav Ghosh
III. Jhumpa Lahiri
IV. Salman Rushdie

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A - I, B - III, C - II, D - IV
A - II, B - IV, C - I, D - III
A - IV, B - I, C - III, D - II
A - III, B - II, C - IV, D - I
items.explanation: Amitav Ghosh authored The Nutmeg's Curse: Parables for a Planet in Crisis (2021, A-II); Salman Rushdie wrote the novel Victory City (2023, B-IV); Amitava Kumar wrote A Time Outside This Time: A Novel (2021, C-I); and Jhumpa Lahiri published the essay collection Translating Myself and Others (2022, D-III).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q2
items.stem: Tolstoy's War and Peace carries a lengthy discussion of determinism and free will in ________
options: an exchange between Pierre and Natasha
an exchange between Nikolai Rostof and Princess Bezukhoi
items.explanation: Leo Tolstoy's War and Peace (1869) concludes with a two-part Epilogue; the entire Second Epilogue is a lengthy philosophical treatise examining the laws of history and the tension between historical determinism (necessity) and individual free will.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q3
items.stem:
Which three of the following writers are associated with 'kitchen sink drama'?
(a) Arnold Wesker
(b) John Arden
(c) Shelagh Delaney
(d) John Osborne
Choose the most appropriate option:
items.explanation: Arnold Wesker (a, Roots), Shelagh Delaney (c, A Taste of Honey), and John Osborne (d, Look Back in Anger) are central playwrights of British 'kitchen sink drama' of the late 1950s, which depicted gritty working-class domestic life.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q4
items.stem:
Using a non - linear narrative, this American novel explores the psychic damage to a veteran
of World War II and shows how a measure of healing is attained through his acceptance of
Laguna myths and rituals. Identify the work
items.explanation: Native American writer Leslie Marmon Silko's novel Ceremony (1977) uses a non-linear narrative interwoven with traditional Pueblo oral poetry to recount how Tayo, a traumatized World War II veteran of the Bataan Death March, finds spiritual healing through Laguna Pueblo rituals.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q5
items.stem:
What is the Chronological order of the appearance of the following periodicals?
(a) The Tatler
(b) The Spectator
(c) The Examiner
(d) The Reflector
Choose the correct option :
items.explanation: The chronological order of appearance is: Richard Steele's The Tatler (a, April 1709), Addison and Steele's The Spectator (b, March 1711), Jonathan Swift's Tory periodical The Examiner (c, August 1710 / or Leigh Hunt's The Examiner, 1808), and Leigh Hunt's quarterly magazine The Reflector (d, 1810–1811).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q6
items.stem: William Empson's Seven Types of Ambiguity is
items.explanation: William Empson's landmark critical study Seven Types of Ambiguity (1930), written while studying under I. A. Richards at Cambridge, is a close-reading analysis of poetic ambivalence and the multiple layers of verbal meaning in English verse.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q7
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The best poetry will be found to have a power of forming, sustaining and delighting us, as nothing else can.
Statement II: No man has ever been a great poet without being, at the same time, a great critic.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
items.explanation: Statement I quotes Matthew Arnold's 'The Study of Poetry' (1880) on the formative power of the best poetry, while Statement II adapts Samuel Taylor Coleridge's remark in Biographia Literaria ('No man was ever yet a great poet, without being at the same time a profound philosopher'); Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q8
items.stem:
Identify
the
critics
and
their
respective works
options: Horace - Ars Poetica Aristotle - Poetics Quintillian - Institutio Oratoria Longinus - On the Sublime Ben Jonson - An Apology for Poetry Sidney - An Essay of Dramatic Poesy Dryden - Discoveries
Horace - Poetics Aristotle - Ars Poetica Quintillian - On the sublime Longinus - Discoveries Ben Jonson - Institutio Oratoria Sidney - An Essay of Dramatic Poesy Dryden - An Apology for Poetry
Horace - On the sublime Aristotle - Poetics Quintillian - Discoveries Longinus - Institutio Oratoria Ben Jonson - An Essay of Dramatic Poesy Sidney - Ars Poetica Dryden - An Apology for Poetry
Horace - Ars Poetica Aristotle - Poetics Quintillian - Institutio Oratoria Ben Jonson - Discoveries Sidney - An Apology for Poetry Dryden - An Essay of Dramatic Poesy
items.explanation: This set accurately pairs each critic with his major treatise: Horace's Ars Poetica, Aristotle's Poetics, Quintilian's Institutio Oratoria, Ben Jonson's Timber, or Discoveries (1640), Sir Philip Sidney's An Apology for Poetry (1595), and John Dryden's An Essay of Dramatic Poesy (1668).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q9
items.stem:
Which two concepts, developed by the French sociologist Pierre Bourdieu, have become increasingly influential in cultural studies?
(a) Dissemination
(b) Gynesis
(c) Cultural Capital
(d) Habitus
Choose the correct option:
items.explanation: French sociologist Pierre Bourdieu developed the influential concepts of 'cultural capital' (c, non-financial social assets like education and taste that promote social mobility) and 'habitus' (d, ingrained habits, skills, and dispositions shaped by social class).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q10
items.stem: Who is the author of the essay, "What Isn't Literature?"?
items.explanation: American literary theorist E.D. Hirsch Jr. authored the essay 'What Isn't Literature?' (published in Paul Hernadi's edited volume What Is Literature?, 1978), arguing against purely essentialist definitions of literary texts.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q11
items.stem:
Match the columns :
Terms
(I) Apollonian – Dionysian
(II) Fancy – Imagination
(III) Hellenism – Hebraism
(IV) Inscape – Instress

Theorists
(1) Matthew Arnold
(2) Friedrich Nietzsche
(3) G.H. Hopkins
(4) S.T. Coleridge

Codes : (I) (II) (III) (IV)
items.explanation: Friedrich Nietzsche formulated the Apollonian–Dionysian duality in The Birth of Tragedy (2), S.T. Coleridge distinguished Fancy and Imagination in Biographia Literaria (4), Matthew Arnold contrasted Hellenism and Hebraism in Culture and Anarchy (1), and Gerard Manley Hopkins coined 'inscape' and 'instress' (3).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q12
items.stem: In which year was R. L. Stevenson's Treasure Island published?
items.explanation: Robert Louis Stevenson's adventure novel Treasure Island was first published in book form by Cassell and Company in November 1883 (following its serialization in the children's magazine Young Folks from 1881 to 1882).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q13
items.stem:
According to Roland Barthes, which of the following "Codes" are common to all narratives?
A. Synthetic code
B. Proairetic code
C. Semic code
D. Hermeneutic code
E. Symbolic code
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D and E only
items.explanation: In S/Z (1970), Roland Barthes identifies five narrative codes: Hermeneutic, Proairetic, Semic, Symbolic, and Cultural/Referential; thus B (Proairetic), C (Semic), D (Hermeneutic), and E (Symbolic) are authentic Barthesian codes (Option 4: B, C, D and E only).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q14
items.stem: Which of the following poems deals with neighbourly relations ?
options: Stopping by Woods on a Snowy Evening
items.explanation: Robert Frost's blank-verse poem 'Mending Wall' (from North of Boston, 1914) explores neighbourly relations through two New England farmers who meet each spring to repair the stone wall between their properties, debating 'Something there is that doesn't love a wall' versus 'Good fences make good neighbours.'

items.title: Mock #14 · Q15
items.stem:
Arrange the following detective novels of Agatha Christie in the correct chronological order of their publication.
A. Death on the Nile
B. Murder in the Orient Express
C. Sparkling Cyanide
D. The Mysterious Affair at Styles
E. The Murder of Roger Ackroyd
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: The chronological publication sequence of Agatha Christie's detective novels is: The Mysterious Affair at Styles (D, 1920), The Murder of Roger Ackroyd (E, 1926), Murder on the Orient Express (B, 1934), Death on the Nile (A, 1937), and Sparkling Cyanide (C, 1945), matching D, E, B, A, C.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q16
items.stem: Which of the following in-text citations is incorrect?
options: According to Naomi Baron, reading is "just half of literacy. The other half is writing" (Baron 194).
Others note that doctors have not yet adequately explained the effects climate change will have on human health (Lemery and Auerbach 4–5).
According to Gao Xingjian, "Literature in essence is divorced from utility" (7).
The author knew Bureau de la Rivière, another of Charles V's executors (Christine 192).
items.explanation: According to the MLA Handbook (9th edition), when an author's name (Naomi Baron) is already stated in the signal phrase within the sentence, repeating the surname in the parenthetical citation '(Baron 194)' is redundant; it should simply be '(194)'.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q17
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: According to Michel Foucault, the French Revolution created grounds for the birth of 'the Clinic'.
Statement II: Foucault mentions that the doctors started caring for the body of the patients the way priests cared for the soul of the sinners.

In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
items.explanation: In The Birth of the Clinic: An Archaeology of Medical Perception (1963), Michel Foucault argues that the institutional and epistemological reorganization around the French Revolution gave rise to modern clinical medicine (Statement I is true) and that medical doctors assumed a quasi-priestly pastoral authority over the body comparable to the clergy's care for souls (Statement II is true).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q18
items.stem:
Which among the following is NOT a
typical "Indian English Poem" by
Nissim Ezekiel ?
options: Goodbye Party for Miss Pushpa T.S
items.explanation: 'The Railway Clerk', 'Goodbye Party for Miss Pushpa T. S.', and 'The Patriot' are famous satirical 'Very Indian Poems in Indian English' by Nissim Ezekiel. 'How the English Lessons Ended' is not by Ezekiel (it is a poem by Sri Lankan-born writer Yasmine Gooneratne).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q19
items.stem:
Identify the novels that were published in the 1980s and the 1990s:
A. Red Earth and Pouring Rain
B. The Circle of Reason
C. The Ghosts of Vasu Master
D. Miguel Street
E. The Siege of Babylon
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D and E only
items.explanation: Vikram Chandra's Red Earth and Pouring Rain (1995, A), Amitav Ghosh's The Circle of Reason (1986, B), and Githa Hariharan's The Ghosts of Vasu Master (1994, C) were published in the 1980s and 1990s, whereas V. S. Naipaul's Miguel Street appeared in 1959 (Option 2: A, B and C only).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q20
items.stem: Who is the best known figure amongst the following for articulating the concept of ‘Negritude’?
items.explanation: Martinican poet and statesman Aimé Césaire coined and articulated the concept of Négritude in the 1930s (most prominently in Cahier d'un retour au pays natal, 1939) alongside Léopold Sédar Senghor and Léon Damas, creating a literary movement that celebrated Black African cultural heritage and resisted French colonial assimilation.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q21
items.stem:
Match the column:
A. Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star
B. Wee Willie Winkie
C. Mary had a Little Lamb
D. Old Mother Hubbard
I. William Miller
II. Jane and Ann Taylor
III. Sarah Catherine Martin
IV. Sarah Josepha Hale
items.explanation: Jane and Ann Taylor composed 'The Star' ('Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star', 1806, A-II), William Miller wrote 'Wee Willie Winkie' (1841, B-I), Sarah Josepha Hale authored 'Mary's Lamb' ('Mary Had a Little Lamb', 1830, C-IV), and Sarah Catherine Martin wrote 'Old Mother Hubbard' (1805, D-III).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q22
items.stem: Which among the following is not written by a sportsperson?
options: A Country Called Childhood: A Memoir
Playing It My Way: My Autobiography
items.explanation: A Country Called Childhood: A Memoir (2022) was written by acclaimed Indian actress, poet, and painter Deepti Naval, whereas Open (2009) is by tennis star Andre Agassi, Unbreakable (2013) is by boxer Mary Kom, and Playing It My Way (2014) is by cricketer Sachin Tendulkar.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q23
items.stem:
From the following writers, who are known for Magic Realism?
A. R.K. Narayan
B. Salman Rushdie
C. V.S. Naipaul
D. Gabriel Garcia Marquez
E. Mulk Raj Anand
items.explanation: Salman Rushdie (notably in Midnight's Children) and Gabriel García Márquez (notably in One Hundred Years of Solitude) are two of world literature's most celebrated exponents of magic realism (B and D). R.K. Narayan, V.S. Naipaul, and Mulk Raj Anand are realist writers who do not write in the magic realist mode.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q24
items.stem: Which of the following is not an award received by Mahasweta Devi ?
items.explanation: Bengali writer and activist Mahasweta Devi (1926–2016) was honoured with the Padma Shri (1986), the Jnanpith Award (1996), and the Ramon Magsaysay Award (1997). Because she wrote in Bengali rather than English, she did not receive the Commonwealth Writers' Prize.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q25
items.stem:
Arrange the following critical works in their chronological order of publication:
A. "Preface to Lyrical Ballads"
B. A Defence of Rhyme
C. "Life of Cowley"
D. "The Frontiers of Criticism"

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The chronological order of publication is: Samuel Daniel's 'A Defence of Ryme' (1603, B); Samuel Johnson's 'Life of Cowley' from Lives of the English Poets (1779, C); William Wordsworth's 'Preface to Lyrical Ballads' (1800 second edition, A); and T.S. Eliot's lecture/essay 'The Frontiers of Criticism' (delivered and published 1956, D).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q26
items.stem: Which of the following poems is quoted as the epigraph to A Raisin in the Sun by Lorraine Hansberry ?
items.explanation: The play's title and epigraph come from Langston Hughes's 'Harlem', which asks 'What happens to a dream deferred?'

items.title: Mock #14 · Q27
items.stem:
Assertion (A) : A quarto refers to a text in which each leaf was a quarter the size of the original sheet.
Reason (R) : Because eight pages of text were printed on large sheets of paper, which were then folded four times to produce four leaves.
In the context of the two statements, which one of the following is correct ?
items.explanation: Assertion (A) is true because a quarto leaf is one-fourth the size of the original printer's sheet. Reason (R) is false because to produce four leaves (eight pages), the sheet is folded twice (not four times).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q28
items.stem: Who among the following declared in 1920 that "there is no longer any intellectual life in England"?
items.explanation: Ezra Pound wrote this in a 1920 letter to William Carlos Williams before departing London for Paris and Italy, declaring that intellectual vitality in England had died out and that provincial conservatism had overtaken the London literary world.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q29
items.stem:
Identify the works written by Richard Brinsley Sheridan:
A. Richelieu
B. St. Patrick's Day
C. The Duenna
D. The Citizen of the World
E. Irene
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The farce St. Patrick's Day; or, The Scheming Lieutenant (1775, B) and the comic opera The Duenna (1775, C) were written by Richard Brinsley Sheridan. Richelieu (1839) is by Edward Bulwer-Lytton, The Citizen of the World (1762) is by Oliver Goldsmith, and Irene (1749) is by Samuel Johnson.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q30
items.stem: Robert Browning’s “My Last Duchess” is an example of :
items.explanation: Robert Browning's 'My Last Duchess' (1842) is a classic dramatic monologue. Through a single continuous speech to an envoy, the Duke of Ferrara unwittingly reveals his jealousy, controlling arrogance, and moral corruption.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q31
items.stem:
Match the column:
(Work)
A. Poverty and Un-British Rule in India
B. The Slave Girl of Agra
C. Love Songs and Elegies
D. Gora
(Author)
I. Romesh Chander Dutt
II. Dadabhai Naoroji
III. Rabindranath Tagore
IV. Manmohan Ghosh
items.explanation: These classic works match their authors: Dadabhai Naoroji authored the landmark economic critique *Poverty and Un-British Rule in India* (A-II, 1901), Romesh Chunder Dutt translated his historical romance *The Slave Girl of Agra* (B-I, 1909), Manmohan Ghose published *Love Songs and Elegies* (C-IV, 1898), and Rabindranath Tagore wrote the novel *Gora* (D-III, 1909).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q32
items.stem: Dev Virahsawmy's Toufann is an adaptation of Shakespeare's play _____.
items.explanation: Mauritian playwright Dev Virahsawmy's Mauritian Creole play Toufann (1991) is a postcolonial adaptation and reimagining of William Shakespeare's The Tempest.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q33
items.stem:
Which two of the following oppositions are best evoked by Hamlet's utterance - "To be or not
to be"?

A. between life and death

B. between action and emotion

C. between affirmation and confirmation

D. between doing and abstaining from doing

Choose the correct answer from the options given below
items.explanation: In Act III, Scene 1 of Shakespeare's Hamlet, Prince Hamlet's soliloquy 'To be, or not to be, that is the question' weighs two fundamental oppositions: the existential choice between life and death (continuing to live versus ending one's life), and the moral dilemma between active resistance ('taking arms') and passive endurance ('abstaining from doing').

items.title: Mock #14 · Q34
items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an example of derivational morpheme ?
items.explanation: Derivational morphemes create new words or alter lexical categories. While '-ship' forms an abstract noun, in the UGC answer key option (1) friend – friendship was designated, distinguishing it from adjectival and participial category-shifting derivations.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q35
items.stem:
Arrange the following poetic lines chronologically in the order of the publication of the poems they appear in:
A. She is the Rose, the glorie of the day,
B. Resembles life what once was deem'd of light,
C. Away! The moor is dark beneath the moon
D. When I consider how my light is spent
E. When in the chronicle of wasted time / I see descriptions of the fairest wights,
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: The lines appear in Edmund Spenser's Daphnaida (1591, A), John Milton's 'When I Consider How My Light Is Spent' (D), William Shakespeare's Sonnet 106 (1609, E), Samuel Taylor Coleridge's 'What Is Life?' (1805/1829, B), and P. B. Shelley's 'Stanzas—April, 1814' (1816, C), matching sequence A, D, E, B, C.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q36
items.stem:
Which of the following feminists has questioned the following?
"Why did men drink wine and women water? Why was one sex so prosperous and the other so poor? What effect has poverty on fiction? What conditions are necessary for the creation of works of art?"
items.explanation: Virginia Woolf poses these famous questions in Chapter 1 of her feminist essay A Room of One's Own (1929), examining how material wealth, social privilege, and economic independence shape women's ability to write fiction.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q37
items.stem:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The Book The Theatre of Revolt was written by Robert Brustein.
Statement II: The Book The Theatre of Revolt is written in the context of French Revolution.
In the light of the statements given above choose the correct answer given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true and Statement II is false
Statement I is false and Statement II is true
items.explanation: Statement I is true and Statement II is false: The Theatre of Revolt (1964) was written by American drama critic Robert Brustein, but it analyzes modern dramatic rebellion in playwrights from Ibsen and Strindberg to Brecht and Genet rather than the French Revolution.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q38
items.stem:
Which ,of ,the ,following ,is ONOT ,a ,school ,associated ,with ,Romantic ,period ,in ,English
literature ?
items.explanation: The Fireside Poets (including Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, William Cullen Bryant, John Greenleaf Whittier, and Oliver Wendell Holmes) were 19th-century American domestic poets, whereas the Lake School, Cockney School, and Satanic School were English Romantic groupings.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q39
items.stem:
Identify the correct statements on Langue and Parole below :
1. Langue is the abstract language system, the grammar of a language.
2. Parole is the language actually produced by its user following langue.
3. Langue is the language actually produced by its users following parole.
4. Parole is the abstract language system, the grammar of a system.
items.explanation: In Ferdinand de Saussure's Course in General Linguistics (1916), langue denotes the shared, abstract grammatical system of a language (1), whereas parole denotes concrete individual speech acts or utterances produced by speakers following that system (2).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q40
items.stem:
The first instance of female cross-dressing with the disconcerting nuances of a boy actor
dressing as a boy while playing the role of a woman in the dramatic world of Shakespeare
occurs in __________
items.explanation: As noted in Andrew Sanders's The Short Oxford History of English Literature, Shakespeare's earliest experiment with female cross-dressing—where a boy actor playing a woman disguises herself as a boy page—occurs in his early comedy The Two Gentlemen of Verona (c. 1589–1591), when Julia dresses as the page Sebastian.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q41
items.meta: Unit IX: Literary Theory Post World War II
items.stem:
Match the items in List – I with items in List – II according to the code given below :
List – I (Theorist)
(i) Michel Foucault
(ii) Judith Butler
(iii) Alan Sinfield
(iv) Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick

List – II (Book)
(1) Gender Trouble
(2) Epistemology of the Closet
(3) History of Sexuality
(4) Cultural Politics-Queer Reading

Which is the correct combination according to the code :
Codes : (i) (ii) (iii) (iv)
items.explanation: Michel Foucault wrote The History of Sexuality (3), Judith Butler wrote Gender Trouble (1), Alan Sinfield wrote Cultural Politics—Queer Reading (4), and Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick wrote Epistemology of the Closet (2).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q42
items.stem:
Identify, from the following list, two plays written by John Webster :

I.
A Woman Killed with Kindness
II.
The Revenger's Tragedy

III. The White Devil
IV.
The Ducchess of Malfi

The right combination according to the code is
items.explanation: John Webster wrote the two great Jacobean revenge tragedies The White Devil (1612) and The Duchess of Malfi (c. 1613–14). A Woman Killed with Kindness (1603) was written by Thomas Heywood, while The Revenger's Tragedy (1607) is attributed to Thomas Middleton.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q43
items.stem:
Which two of the following are associated with Deconstruction?
(a) Jacques Derrida
(b) Raymond Williams
(c) Paul de Man
(d) Jonathan Dollimore
Choose the correct option:
items.explanation: French philosopher Jacques Derrida (a) originated the theory of Deconstruction in works like Of Grammatology (1967), and Yale School critic Paul de Man (c) championed deconstructive rhetorical reading in America. Raymond Williams and Jonathan Dollimore are associated with Cultural Materialism.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q44
items.stem: Who is the narrator in Kamala Markandaya's Nectar in a Sieve ?
items.explanation: Kamala Markandaya's classic Indian English novel Nectar in a Sieve (1954) is narrated in the first person by Rukmani, a resilient peasant woman who looks back on her life of rural hardship, famine, and love with her tenant-farmer husband Nathan.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q45
items.stem:
Arrange the following steps of material collection according to hierarchy given by Delia da Sousa Correa and W.R. Owens in The Handbook to Literary Research:
A. Identify your nearest major research library
B. Visit your own university library
C. Identify what is available online
D. Visit your nearest major research library
items.explanation: In *The Handbook to Literary Research*, Delia da Sousa Correa and W. R. Owens define a four-step hierarchy for collecting secondary materials: first identify what is available online (C), consult your own university library (B), identify your nearest major research library (A), and finally visit that major research library in person (D).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q46
items.stem: The library where the "Battle of Books" takes place is _______
items.explanation: Jonathan Swift's mock-heroic prose satire The Battle of the Books (1704) depicts a literal battle between ancient and modern books inside St. James's Library in London, where the classical scholar Richard Bentley served as Keeper of the Royal Libraries.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q47
items.stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as
Reason R

Assertion A: Research methods are a range of tools that are used for different types of
inquiry.

Reason R: The tools used in research are products of the situations in which they are applied.
In light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Ais false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Ais true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
items.explanation: In research methodology, research methods comprise a diverse range of analytical, qualitative, and quantitative tools employed for different kinds of inquiry. This diversity exists precisely because research tools are shaped by and adapted to the specific disciplinary contexts and practical situations in which they are applied.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q48
items.stem: "It is significant that the productive capacities of this Third Space have a colonial or postcolonial provenance". The above lines have been written by
items.explanation: Postcolonial theorist Homi K. Bhabha wrote this famous sentence on cultural hybridity and the 'Third Space of enunciation' in his essay 'The Commitment to Theory' in The Location of Culture (1994).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q49
items.stem:
Gilles Deleuze and Félix Guattari's Anti-Oedipus: Capitalism and Schizophrenia fuses two theoretical paradigms. They are
A. Marxism
B. Poststructuralism
C. Psychoanalysis
D. Feminism
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In Anti-Oedipus: Capitalism and Schizophrenia (1972), French philosopher Gilles Deleuze and psychoanalyst Felix Guattari fuse Marxism (A) and Psychoanalysis (C) into 'schizoanalysis', critiquing both Freudian Oedipal repression and capitalist social production.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q50
items.stem:
In which poem does Matthew Arnold express the dilemma of :
"Wandering between two worlds, one dead, The other powerless to be born" ?
items.explanation: These famous lines appear in Matthew Arnold's poem 'Stanzas from the Grande Chartreuse' (1855), where the speaker visits a Carthusian monastery and laments the Victorian crisis of faith caught between dead medieval belief and an unborn modern age.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q51
items.stem:
Match the characters with the novels of Amitav Ghosh in which they appear according to the code given below :
List – I (Characters)
(i) Fakir
(ii) Tridip
(iii) Rajkumar
(iv) Murugan

List – II (Novels)
(1) The Glass Palace
(2) The Hungry Tide
(3) The Calcutta Chromosome
(4) Shadow Lines

Codes : (i) (ii) (iii) (iv)

items.title: Mock #14 · Q52
items.stem: Which statement rightly defines split infinitive?
options: Astructure in which an adverb follows to-infinitive
Astructure in which an adjective comes between 'to' and the rest of the infinitive
Astructure in which an adjective comes before bare infinitive
Astructure in which an adverb comes between 'to' and the rest of the infinitive
items.explanation: A split infinitive occurs when an adverb or adverbial phrase is placed between the particle 'to' and the bare infinitive verb, as in the famous phrase 'to boldly go'. Traditional prescriptivists discouraged this construction, though it is widely used in modern English.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q57

items.stem: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Reason (R): Foucault defines discourse as the material manifestation of thought which shapes our subjectivity. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
items.explanation: In Michel Foucault's archaeology and genealogy, discourses are not mere abstract linguistic constructs but embodied, material practices governed by historical rules that construct and discipline social reality and human subjectivity, making Reason (R) the precise theoretical foundation and explanation for Assertion (A).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q58

items.explanation: British sociologist Roland Robertson popularized the concept of 'glocalization' (adapted from the Japanese business term dochakuka) in his book Globalization: Social Theory and Global Culture (1992) and his 1995 essay 'Glocalization: Time-Space and Homogeneity-Heterogeneity', describing the simultaneous interpenetration of global and local cultures.

“Logic cannot have any empirical part”, because:
A. laws of thought are subjective.
B. it propounds laws whose applicability can be shown.
C. its laws are valid for all thought.
D. its laws are valid for everyone's experience.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In the preface to Immanuel Kant's Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals (1785), Kant explains that formal logic cannot have an empirical part because its universal laws of thought do not rest on sensory experience. Instead, its laws are universally valid for all thinking (C) and are capable of strict demonstration (B).

items.title: Mock #14 · Q95
items.stem:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow:

Logic cannot have any empirical part; that is, a part in which the universal and necessary laws of thought should rest on grounds taken from experience; otherwise it would not be logic, i.e, a canon for the understanding or the reason, valid for all thought, and capable of demonstration. Natural and moral philosophy, on the contrary, can each have their empirical part, since the former has to determine the laws of nature as an object of experience; the latter, the laws of the human will, so far as it is affected by nature: the former, however, being laws according to which everything does happen; the latter, laws according to which everything ought to happen. Ethics, however, must also consider the conditions under which what ought to happen frequently does not.
- Immanuel Kant

Based on the given passage which two of the following statements are correct?
A. For natural philosophy, nature influences the laws.
B. For moral philosophy, nature is to be experienced.
C. Natural philosophy does not describe how things actually do happen.
D. Moral philosophy accounts for what should be.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
items.explanation: In the passage from Kant's Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals, natural philosophy (physics) is governed by laws of nature that determine how things actually happen (A), whereas moral philosophy (ethics) is governed by laws of freedom that account for how things ought to happen—'what should be' (D).

items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow:

And the creature run from the cur?
There thou mightst behold the great image of authority: a dog’s obeyed in office. —
Thou rascal beadle, hold thy bloody hand!
Why dost thou lash that whore? Strip thine own back;
Thou hotly lust’st to use her in that kind
For which thou whipp’st her. The usurer hangs the cozener.
Through tatter'd clothes small vices do appear;
Robes and furr'd gowns hide all. Plate sin with gold,
And the strong lance of justice hurtless breaks;
Arm it in rags, a pigmy’s straw doth pierce it.
- Shakespeare, King Lear

Who speaks these lines and to whom?
items.explanation: King Lear speaks these lines to the blinded Earl of Gloucester when they meet near Dover in Act IV, Scene 6 of Shakespeare's King Lear. In his madness, Lear delivers a searing indictment of corrupt judges, hypocritical beadles, and the double standards of wealth and justice.

In the passage, the church officer is asked to whip his own back rather than the prostitute's because:
options: as a religious man he should punish himself for others' sins
he does not have the authority to whip a woman
men like him make them prostitutes
he at one time had lusted after her
items.explanation: In Act IV, Scene 6 of Shakespeare's King Lear, Lear tells the 'rascal beadle' (parish officer) to strip and whip his own back rather than the prostitute's because the officer secretly lusts to commit the very act with her for which he punishes her ('Thou hotly lust'st to use her in that kind / For which thou whipp'st her').

The two sentences in the lines from "Through tatter'd clothes..." to "...straw doth pierce it" deal with two foibles, (i) vice and (ii) sin. About these two, the speaker says that:
options: Vice afflicts all but sin afflicts only the weak
Sin afflicts all but vice afflicts only the strong
Sin and vice are palpable in the weak and impalpable in the strong
Sin and vice are seen in both the weak and the strong
items.explanation: In Lear's speech ('Through tatter'd clothes small vices do appear; / Robes and furr'd gowns hide all. Plate sin with gold, / And the strong lance of justice hurtless breaks; / Arm it in rags, a pigmy's straw doth pierce it'), Shakespeare contrasts poverty and wealth: sin and vice are exposed and punished in the poor and weak, but concealed and protected in the rich and powerful.

items.title: Mock #14 · Q99
items.meta: Unit IV / Unit VIII: Prose & Criticism
items.stem:
Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow:

The surgeon deposited it in her arms. She imprinted her cold, white lips passionately on its forehead; passed her hands over her face; gazed wildly around; shuddered; fell back — and died. They chafed her breast, hands, temples; but the blood had stopped forever. They talked of hope and comfort. They had been strangers too long. ‘It's all over, Mrs. Thingummy!’, said the surgeon at last.
- Dickens, Oliver Twist

In the expression, "passed her hands over her face", the 'face' is of:
items.explanation: In Chapter 1 of Charles Dickens's Oliver Twist (1838), the dying young mother Agnes Fleming ('the patient') kisses her newborn baby ('imprinted her cold, white lips passionately on its forehead') and then 'passed her hands over her face; gazed wildly round; shuddered; fell back—and died.' Since the infant is referred to as 'it', 'her face' refers to the face of the patient herself.

They chafed her breast, hands, temples; but the blood had stopped forever. They talked of hope and comfort. They had been strangers too long. ‘It's all over, Mrs. Thingummy!’, said the surgeon at last.
- Dickens, Oliver Twist

The implication of "they had been strangers too long" is:
options: Those who spoke of 'hope and comfort' had been strangers too long.
'Hope and comfort' had been stranger to the patient too long.
'Hope' had been stranger to 'comfort' for too long.
'Hope and comfort' had been strangers to the surgeon, nurse and the patient too long.
items.explanation: In Chapter 1 of Charles Dickens's Oliver Twist, as the parish surgeon and pauper nurse attend the dying young mother, Dickens writes: 'They talked of hope and comfort. They had been strangers too long.' The narrator implies that 'hope and comfort' were complete strangers to the destitute young mother, whose long suffering in life had placed her far beyond the reach of earthly consolation.
